newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TURKISH POLITICIAN PUNCHED IN HUNGARY HOTEL.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH POLITICIAN PUNCHED IN HUNGARY HOTEL.

text.p: A Turkish politician drinking coffee in a luxury Budapest hotel was punched in the face and had his nose bloodied by an unknown assailant, Hungarian police said on Monday.

Mesut Yilmaz, leader of the opposition Motherland Party (ANAP), was approached by three men in the lobby of the Hilton Hotel early on Sunday evening and one of them punched him in the face, causing his nose to start bleeding, police said.
Police said the hotel notified them of the attack but Yilmaz had declined to give details of the incident.
"He said he would settle the case in Turkey," police captain Gyorgy Kapin told Reuters.
Yilmaz checked out of the hotel and could not be reached for comment. Hotel officials said the Turkish embassy in Budapest had asked them not to divulge details.
Yilmaz was quoted by Turkey's semi-official Anatolian news agency as saying that his assailant fled after the attack.
"I was having coffee in the hotel lobby when someone I don't know came up and punched me," Yilmaz told Anatolian. "I don't know if he was a Turk or not."
The agency quoted a businessman accompanying Yilmaz as saying the attack was related to Yilmaz's role in exposing a security scandal that has rocked Turkey.
